value_stream.name: On-Site Renewable Energy & Prosumer Asset Operations

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), O&M Vendor, BI (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Volume: ~80 commissioned solar sites today, growing toward the ~205-rooftop potential (per the README)

workflows.name: Daily Generation Monitoring, SCADA & Performance Surveillance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor generation via SCADA/monitoring platform" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-dispatch of "Energy Manager detect and triage under-performance/anomalies" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-match of "Energy Manager publish the daily/weekly generation and performance report" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-135 (ensure renewable asset registration & net-metering settlement.)
- operational: SCADA and anomaly detection; operational: smart alerting and prioritization
Pain Points / Risks: - **Monitoring-blindspot risk**: Undetected under-performance erodes savings; mitigated by SCADA and anomaly detection
- **Alert-fatigue risk**: Too many alarms cause ignoring; mitigated by smart alerting and prioritization
System Touchpoints: - SCADA/monitoring platform; BI (links to VS-28.1); energy/asset management; facility (links to VS-20.3)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/Facilities monitor generation via SCADA/monitoring platform: real-time kW/kWh, performance ratio, inverter status, alarms, and per-string performance across all sites; aggregate to portfolio view in BI (links to VS-28.1)

Energy Manager detect and triage under-performance/anomalies (soiling, shading, string/inverter fault, degradation) vs expected yield (W3456); prioritize by impact and dispatch O&M (W3459) or warranty (W3460)

Energy Manager publish the daily/weekly generation and performance report (actual vs expected, availability, faults), feed consumption-vs-generation matching (W3458) and net-metering settlement (W3463), and report portfolio performance to governance (W3471)

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, Facilities (links to VS-20.3/VS-07), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Finance (links to VS-17)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "profile site load vs generation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "optimize self-consumption" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "measure savings achieved" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-554 (ensure controlled execution — Generation Operations, Grid Interaction & Net-Metering (PA-108.2).)
- operational: load-shifting and BESS; operational: coordination and guardrails
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-self-consumption risk**: Exporting cheap and importing expensive erodes savings; mitigated by load-shifting and BESS
- **Disruption risk**: Load-shifting harms store operations/comfort; mitigated by coordination and guardrails
System Touchpoints: - SCADA/BMS (links to VS-20.3); energy analytics (links to VS-28.1); store/DC ops (links to VS-07/VS-04); finance/savings (links to VS-17)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/Analytics profile site load vs generation: consumption pattern (store/DC load, HVAC, lighting, refrigeration links to VS-20.3), generation curve, self-consumption ratio, and export volume; identify load-shifting and sizing opportunities

Energy Manager/Facilities optimize self-consumption (highest-value use of generated kWh): load-shifting (HVAC, water heating, charging) to solar hours, BESS charge/discharge scheduling (W3460), and avoidance of peak/grid import where tariffs penalize it; coordinate with store/DC ops (links to VS-07/VS-04)

Energy Manager/Finance measure savings achieved (self-consumed kWh × avoided tariff + export kWh × export rate per W3463), validate against the business case (W3451), and tune the optimization as tariffs/load change; report to the performance review (W3471)

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), O&M Vendor, HSE (links to VS-24)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "checks, thermography, inverter service, BESS maintenance" field work (replaces manual Step 2 planning).
- System auto-document of "O&M Vendor/Facilities execute scheduled PM and reactive troubleshooting" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Energy Manager verify O&M completion and performance recovery, capture" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-554 (ensure controlled execution — Generation Operations, Grid Interaction & Net-Metering (PA-108.2).)
- operational: cleaning PM and soiling analytics; operational: SLA and scorecard (links to VS-67)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Soiling/under-performance risk**: Uncleaned modules under-perform; mitigated by cleaning PM and soiling analytics
- **O&M-vendor-SLA risk**: Poor vendor response extends downtime; mitigated by SLA and scorecard (links to VS-67)
System Touchpoints: - Asset/PM register (links to VS-35/W400); facility PM (links to VS-20.3/W240); HSE (links to VS-24); service-provider (links to VS-34.2)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/Facilities maintain the O&M plan: scheduled preventive maintenance (module cleaning, torque checks, thermography, inverter service, BESS maintenance), spare-parts inventory, and the O&M vendor SLA (links to VS-34.2 service-provider management); align to facility PM (links to VS-20.3/W240)

O&M Vendor/Facilities execute scheduled PM and reactive troubleshooting (dispatched from W3457 alerts): cleaning, component repair/replacement, electrical/mechanical checks, and HSE compliance (links to VS-24 working-at-height, electrical safety); document work

Energy Manager verify O&M completion and performance recovery, capture maintenance history in the asset register (links to VS-35/W400), track O&M cost vs budget, and feed reliability data to the performance review (W3471) and asset-renewal planning (links to VS-35)

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, O&M, Vendor (manufacturer), Procurement (links to VS-03.3), Finance (links to VS-15)

workflows.name: Inverter / BESS Fault Management & Vendor Warranty Resolution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs and on-site inspection" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validate performance recovery, capture the fault/resolution in the asset history" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-554 (ensure controlled execution — Generation Operations, Grid Interaction & Net-Metering (PA-108.2).)
- operational: spare pool and SLA; operational: serial/warranty tracking and claims
Pain Points / Risks: - **Extended-downtime risk**: Long RMA lead time loses generation; mitigated by spare pool and SLA
- **Warranty-leakage risk**: Out-of-warranty spend not recovered; mitigated by serial/warranty tracking and claims
System Touchpoints: - SCADA/monitoring; asset/warranty register (links to VS-35/W399); vendor/procurement (links to VS-03.3); AP/warranty recovery (links to VS-15/W244)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/O&M diagnose the inverter/BESS fault from SCADA logs and on-site inspection: error code, root cause (hardware, firmware, grid event), warranty status (W3453 serials), and impact; document the case

Energy Manager/Procurement engage the manufacturer/vendor for warranty repair/replacement or out-of-warranty fix: RMA, lead time, cost, and authorization; manage a spare-inverter pool to minimize downtime

Energy Manager restore the asset, validate performance recovery, capture the fault/resolution in the asset history (links to VS-35), and feed recurring failures to procurement/quality (links to VS-31/VS-67) and reliability analytics (W3471); recover warranty cost (links to VS-15/W244)

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Store/DC Ops (links to VS-07/VS-04), HSE (links to VS-24)
fields.Trigger: Grid outage/brownout (links to VS-07/W470); islanding capability

workflows.name: Grid Outage / Brownout Resilience & Islanding Operations

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logic, and compliance with DU/ERC anti-islanding rules" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with store/DC ops" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate post-outage grid reconnection and system recovery, capture resilience…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-554 (ensure controlled execution — Generation Operations, Grid Interaction & Net-Metering (PA-108.2).)
- operational: certified grid-forming setup and DU sign-off (W3462); operational: critical-load sizing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Anti-islanding-compliance risk**: Unauthorized islanding endangers DU workers; mitigated by certified grid-forming setup and DU sign-off (W3462)
- **Resilience-overbuild risk**: Over-investing in islanding beyond critical-load need; mitigated by critical-load sizing
System Touchpoints: - SCADA/islanding control; BCP (links to VS-26); store/DC ops (links to VS-07/VS-04/W470); HSE (links to VS-24)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/Facilities design islanding/resilience capability where justified: grid-forming inverter + BESS, critical-load prioritization (POS links to VS-08, lighting, refrigeration, safety), transfer/islanding logic, and compliance with DU/ERC anti-islanding rules (links to W3462)

During a grid outage, the system islands (if equipped) or the site falls back to generator/UPS (links to VS-07/W470); Facilities/Ops manage the switchover, confirm critical loads sustained, and coordinate with store/DC ops (links to VS-07/VS-04) and HSE (links to VS-24)

Energy Manager/Facilities validate post-outage grid reconnection and system recovery, capture resilience performance (uptime sustained, kWh served), and report resilience value vs the business case (W3451) and BCP (links to VS-26); tune islanding logic

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, Compliance/Regulatory (links to VS-22), Legal (links to VS-100.3), DU, ERC

workflows.name: ERC / DU Interconnection, Net-Metering Registration & Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-submit of "submit application, specs, single-line diagram, structural/electrical…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-import of "import/export meter installation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "inspections, meter calibration, rule changes" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-135 (ensure renewable asset registration & net-metering settlement.)
- operational: early application and DU relationship; operational: regulatory monitoring (links to VS-22)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Registration-delay risk**: Late DU/ERC approval delays energization and savings; mitigated by early application and DU relationship
- **Rule-change risk**: Net-metering/export-pricing changes alter economics; mitigated by regulatory monitoring (links to VS-22.3) and scenario planning
System Touchpoints: - Regulatory/permit (links to VS-22.1/W54); legal (links to VS-100.3); meter/SCADA; multi-region compliance (links to VS-76)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/Compliance register the renewable system with the DU and ERC for net-metering (RE Act / net-metering rules): submit application, specs, single-line diagram, structural/electrical certification, and fees; secure the Certificate of Completion and net-metering agreement

Energy Manager/Legal execute the net-metering/interconnection agreement with the DU: import/export meter installation (bi-directional), export pricing/terms, compliance with DU/ERC technical standards, and anti-islanding; ensure multi-site consistency across DUs/regions (links to VS-76)

Compliance/Energy Manager monitor ongoing regulatory compliance: DU inspections, meter calibration, rule changes (net-metering caps, export pricing, RE Act amendments links to VS-22.3), and reporting; manage renewals and disputes (links to VS-100)

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, Finance/AP (links to VS-15/VS-17), Facilities, DU
fields.Trigger: Monthly DU billing cycle; generation/consumption data (W3457)

workflows.name: Net-Metering Settlement, Export Billing & Import/Export Reconciliation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "validate meter readings and rate application" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-allocate of "allocate cost to the correct entity/site" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Energy Manager/Finance compute the net savings" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-135 (ensure renewable asset registration & net-metering settlement.)
- operational: reconciliation and dispute (links to VS-90); operational: self-consumption optimization (W3458)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Billing-error risk**: DU mis-billing (wrong rate, meter error) over-charges; mitigated by reconciliation and dispute (links to VS-90)
- **Export-rate-volatility risk**: Changing export pricing alters net-metering value; mitigated by self-consumption optimization (W3458)
System Touchpoints: - SCADA/meter; AP/GL (links to VS-15.1/VS-17.1); DU billing; cost allocation (links to VS-72)

steps.activity: Energy Manager/Finance reconcile the monthly DU bill against SCADA/meter data: import kWh (billed at retail tariff), export kWh (credited at export rate), net position, demand charges, and other charges; validate meter readings and rate application

Finance/AP process the net-metered electricity bill (links to VS-15.1/W7), post the electricity expense (reduced by self-generation) and export credit to GL (links to VS-17.1), and resolve billing disputes with the DU (links to VS-90/W244); allocate cost to the correct entity/site (links to VS-72)

Energy Manager/Finance compute the net savings (avoided import + export credit − charges vs baseline grid-only) per site and portfolio, validate against the business case (W3451) and optimization (W3458), and report to the performance review (W3471)

fields.Participants: Energy Manager, HSE (links to VS-24), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Insurance (links to VS-26), Legal (links to VS-100)
fields.Trigger: Safety incident; structural/equipment damage; extreme weather (links to VS-69)

workflows.name: Renewable Asset Safety, Structural & Insurance Incident Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "report per HSE" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document, and remediate" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "update the asset record" from generation telemetry (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-135 (ensure renewable asset registration & net-metering settlement.)
- operational: protection, inspection, and HSE protocol; operational: structural design, insurance, and preparedness
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire/electrical-safety risk**: PV faults can cause fire/shock; mitigated by protection, inspection, and HSE protocol
- **Storm-damage risk**: Typhoons (links to VS-69) damage arrays; mitigated by structural design, insurance, and preparedness
System Touchpoints: - HSE/incident (links to VS-24/W330); insurance claims (links to VS-26.3/W59); asset register (links to VS-35); risk (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: On incident (module damage, fire, structural, electrical, fall, storm damage links to VS-69), Facilities/HSE secure the site, isolate the affected array, ensure personnel/public safety, and report per HSE (links to VS-24) and incident protocol (links to W330/W471)

Energy Manager/HSE investigate root cause (equipment defect, installation, weather, maintenance), document, and remediate (repair/replacement via O&M W3459 or warranty W3460); implement corrective action and feed to HSE/quality learning (links to VS-24/VS-31)

Energy Manager/Insurance file the insurance claim for covered damage (links to VS-26.3/W59 policy lifecycle/claims), recover cost, and update the asset record (links to VS-35); report material incidents to executives (links to VS-33.2) and audit/risk (links to VS-21.2)
